entities.name: Zhejiang University
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Zhejiang University (ZJU), founded in 1897, is one of China's oldest and most prestigious institutions of higher education, located in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province. It plays a pivotal role in advancing educational standards and research capabilities in East Asia and beyond, contributing significantly to China's modern educational landscape. Key figures in its history include President Wu Yifang, who led the university during its formative years, and figures involved in the Project 211 and Project 985 initiatives, which aimed to cultivate world-class universities in China.

Since its inception, Zhejiang University has undergone numerous transformations, starting from its original establishment as a private agricultural school to becoming a comprehensive university with a broad array of disciplines. The university's involvement in national initiatives like Project 211 and Project 985 has propelled it into the ranks of elite educational institutions, allowing it to expand its research output significantly. ZJU has invested heavily in international collaborations and partnerships, resulting in a vibrant academic community that engages in groundbreaking research across various fields, including science, technology, engineering, and humanities.

The legacy of Zhejiang University is evident in its contributions to China's rapid technological advancement and its role in shaping the country's higher education landscape. As a leader in innovation, ZJU has produced influential alumni who have impacted various sectors, both domestically and internationally. Its commitment to research and development has not only enhanced its academic reputation but also fostered economic growth and technological progress in the region.
